name: Ghana
tagline: The forts, the forest and the highlife
summary: The most straightforward country in West Africa to travel, with the Atlantic slave forts of the coast, the Ashanti kingdom at Kumasi, Mole's elephants in the north, and a music scene worth planning around.

entries.caption: The Forts, the Forest and the Highlife
entries.description: Coastal forts, Ashanti gold, elephants in the north, and a band playing somewhere every night.
entries.subject: the white walls of Cape Coast castle above the Atlantic

entries.caption: Coast to Savanna
entries.description: Rainforest and lagoon in the south, transitional woodland through the middle, savanna at Mole.
entries.subject: rainforest canopy in Kakum national park

entries.caption: Mole and Ankasa
entries.description: Elephants that walk into the camp waterhole at Mole, and forest elephants at Ankasa.
entries.subject: elephants at the waterhole below Mole motel

entries.caption: Walking Safari at Mole
entries.description: One of the few parks in West Africa where the game drive is done on foot, with an armed ranger.
entries.subject: a ranger leading walkers through savanna at Mole

entries.caption: The Akwapim and Afadja
entries.description: Afadjato is 885 metres and the highest point, walkable in a morning from Liati Wote.
entries.subject: the green hills of the Volta region from Afadjato

entries.caption: Wli
entries.description: The highest falls in West Africa, dropping out of forest on the Togo border, with bats overhead.
entries.subject: the Wli waterfall dropping through forest in the Volta region

entries.caption: Lake Volta
entries.description: The largest reservoir on earth by surface area, with ferries that take a full day to cross it.
entries.subject: fishing boats on Lake Volta at first light

entries.caption: Busua and Cape Three Points
entries.description: Surf at Busua, and the point where the country runs out into the Gulf of Guinea.
entries.subject: palms above the beach at Busua on the Ghanaian coast

entries.caption: Kakum
entries.description: Rainforest with a canopy walkway thirty metres up, strung between seven emergent trees.
entries.subject: the canopy walkway suspended above Kakum rainforest

entries.caption: Canopy, Surf and Lake
entries.description: The Kakum walkway, Busua's beach breaks, and hiking the Volta hills to the Togo border.
entries.subject: a hiking trail through the hills of the Volta region

entries.caption: Ashanti
entries.description: A kingdom that fought the British to a standstill, and still keeps its own court at Kumasi.
entries.subject: the Manhyia palace grounds at Kumasi

entries.caption: The Ewe and the Dagomba
entries.description: Kente weaving in Volta and Ashanti, and the Dagbon drumming traditions of the north.
entries.subject: a weaver working a kente loom in Bonwire

entries.caption: Jollof, Banku and Grilled Tilapia
entries.description: The jollof argument is unwinnable; the tilapia off the grill with banku settles it.
entries.subject: grilled tilapia and banku served at a roadside chop bar

entries.caption: Homowo and Chale Wote
entries.description: Homowo in Accra in August, and the Chale Wote street art festival in Jamestown.
entries.subject: a street art festival crowd in Jamestown, Accra

entries.caption: Kente and Adinkra
entries.description: Kente woven in strips at Bonwire, and adinkra symbols stamped by hand at Ntonso.
entries.subject: adinkra symbols being stamped onto cloth by hand

entries.caption: The Slave Forts
entries.description: Cape Coast and Elmina — the doors of no return, kept as they were and not softened.
entries.subject: the door of no return at Elmina castle

entries.caption: The Year of Return
entries.description: Ghana asked the diaspora to come back, and a great many people did.
entries.subject: a memorial gathering at Cape Coast castle

entries.caption: Accra and Kumasi
entries.description: Accra on the Atlantic, and Kumasi's Kejetia — one of the largest markets in West Africa.
entries.subject: the vast Kejetia market spread out at Kumasi

entries.caption: Posuban and Colonial Coast
entries.description: The Fante posuban shrines, and the trading architecture strung along the coast road.
entries.subject: a painted Fante posuban shrine in a coastal town

entries.caption: Chop Bars and Trotros
entries.description: The country runs on shared minibuses and roadside kitchens, and both are worth using.
entries.subject: a busy trotro station in Accra

entries.caption: Easy First Africa
entries.description: English-speaking, short distances, and about as gentle an introduction as the continent offers.
entries.subject: children playing on a beach on the Ghanaian coast

entries.caption: Surf, Hike, Paddle
entries.description: Busua's breaks, the Volta hills, and canoes on the lake at Dodi.
entries.subject: a surfer walking out at Busua beach

entries.caption: Lodges on the Water
entries.description: Small lodges above the beach at Busua and Axim, and the Mole escarpment rooms over the waterhole.
entries.subject: a lodge terrace overlooking the waterhole at Mole

entries.caption: Community Forest
entries.description: The Wechiau hippo sanctuary and the Boabeng-Fiema monkey sanctuary, both village-run.
entries.subject: hippos in the Black Volta at the Wechiau sanctuary

entries.caption: Colour Everywhere
entries.description: Kente, market cloth and painted trotros — nothing here is any colour by accident.
entries.subject: stacked bolts of printed cloth in a Ghanaian market

entries.caption: Nzulezo
entries.description: A village built entirely on stilts over Lake Tandane, reached only by canoe.
entries.subject: the stilt village of Nzulezo over the water

entries.caption: The Gentle Introduction
entries.description: English, good roads, a short flight from Europe, and everything within a day's drive.
entries.subject: a coastal road running along the Gulf of Guinea
